the impact of HIV/AIDS and the associated stigma on the mental health of pregnant women in rural South Africa.
the use of efavirenze during pregnancy and its association with suicidal ideation in the postpartum period.

the study findings support the use of alternative antiretroviral agents for the management for HIV during pregnancy, and that efavirenz is contraindicate for the treatment of HIV in women with depression.
efavirenz should be used with caution in patients with a history of depression, as it has been associated with increased suicidal ideation.
there is an association of suicidal ideation with efavirenz use during pregnancy, and this association is independent of the effect of antenatal depression.

efavirenz use during pregnancy is associated with suicidal ideation 1 year postnatally.

we found that women who were on efavirenz during pregnancy were more likely to experience suicidal ideation at 12 months postpartum, controlling for other risk factors such as antenatal depression and intimate partner violence (physical and/or psychological).
the use of efavirenze during pregnancy is associated with postpartum suicidal ideation in rural South Africa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
efavirenz is associated with an increased risk of suicidal ideation in postpartum women.
the use of efavirenze during pregnancy in women living with HIV is associated with suicidal ideation 1-year postpartum.
the use of efavirenze in pregnant women with depression is associated with suicidal ideation postpartum.
